title: Cap. V Obj. 5: predestination without foresight of faith fights the nature and titles of eternal life
latin: Obj. 5. Praedestinatio quae supponitur facta non ex praevisione fidei, pugnat cum natura vitae aeternae, et titulis quibus illa in Scripturis insignitur: Vocatur haereditas filiorum (at soli credentes sunt), merces, praemium, corona justitiae: Ergo non destinatur cuiquam citra omnem considerationem et intuitum fidei et obedientiae.
pass_a: Objection 5. Predestination which is supposed made not from foresight of faith fights with the nature of eternal life, and with the titles by which it is marked in the Scriptures: It is called the inheritance of sons (but only believers are), a wage, a reward, a crown of justice: Therefore it is not destinated to anyone apart from all consideration and intuition of faith and obedience.
pass_b: Obj. 5. Predestination supposed without foresight of faith fights the nature of eternal life and the titles Scripture gives it: inheritance of sons (but only believers are), wage, reward, crown of justice. Therefore it is destinated to no one apart from all consideration and intuition of faith and obedience.

lemmas.gloss: fights the nature of eternal life

title: Cap. V Obj. 5 Sol: enter life as adopted son; predestination tends on a child of wrath
latin: Sol. Natura sive conditio vitae aeternae talis est, ut nemo in eam ingredi possit nisi qui antecedenter factus fuerit actu filius Dei per Spiritum adoptionis: at non est talis, ut nemo ad eam praedestinari possit nisi qui antecedenter fuerit filius Dei adoptatus. Praedestinatio enim continet propositum assumendi in filium: Tendit igitur in filium irae, quem praedestinando facit vas misericordiae quoad propositum; justificando, sanctificando, glorificando facit vas misericordiae quoad actum. Recte igitur requiritur fides antecedanea, aut saltem concomitans, ad constituendum filium actu adoptatum: at perperam requiritur fides antecedanea, ad constituendum Dei decretum de singulari persona adoptanda, et ad haereditatem destinanda.
pass_a: Solution. The nature or condition of eternal life is such that no one can enter into it unless he has antecedently been made actually a son of God through the Spirit of adoption: but it is not such that no one can be predestinated to it unless he has antecedently been an adopted son of God. For predestination contains the purpose of assuming into sonship: It therefore tends upon a son of wrath, whom by predestinatinating it makes a vessel of mercy as to purpose; by justifying, sanctifying, glorifying it makes a vessel of mercy as to act. Rightly therefore is antecedent faith required, or at least concomitant, for constituting a son actually adopted: but wrongly is antecedent faith required for constituting God's decree concerning a singular person to be adopted, and to be destinated to the inheritance.
pass_b: Sol. Eternal life's nature is such that no one can enter it unless antecedently made actually a son of God by the Spirit of adoption — but not such that no one can be predestinated to it unless already an adopted son. Predestination contains the purpose of assuming into sonship: it tends on a child of wrath, whom by predestinatinating it makes a vessel of mercy as to purpose; by justifying, sanctifying, glorifying, a vessel of mercy as to act. Antecedent faith (or at least concomitant) is rightly required to constitute a son actually adopted; wrongly required to constitute God's decree about adopting a singular person and destinating the inheritance.

lemmas.gloss: child of wrath made vessel of mercy
actual adoption vs decree to adopt

title: Cap. V Obj. 5 Sol: titles — eternal life a wage of faith; predestination never called a wage
latin: De titulis respondemus: Vitam aeternam dici mercedem, sive coronam fidei et obedientiae, sed ipsam praedestinationem ad vitam nunquam dici mercedem aut coronam sive fidei sive obedientiae nostrae. Vita aeterna dicitur merces fidei et bonorum operum quia credentibus et sancte viventibus ex promissione sive stipulatione Divina reddenda donatur: at beneficium praedestinationis nunquam sub ulla conditione fidei a nobis antecedente promissum ostenditur. Frustra igitur haec objiciuntur.
pass_a: Concerning the titles we answer: That eternal life is called a wage, or crown of faith and obedience, but predestination itself to life is never called a wage or crown either of our faith or of our obedience. Eternal life is called a wage of faith and of good works because it is gifted as to be rendered to believers and those living holily from a Divine promise or stipulation: but the benefit of predestination is never shown promised under any condition of faith antecedent from us. In vain therefore are these things objected.
pass_b: On the titles we reply: Scripture calls eternal life a wage or crown of faith and obedience — never predestination itself a wage or crown of our faith or obedience. Eternal life is that wage because God gifts it as something to be rendered, by promise or stipulation, to believers who live holy lives. Predestination as a benefit is never shown as promised under any condition of faith coming first from us. These objections therefore fail.

lemmas.gloss: life a wage; predestination never so called
